name: Google
note: One of the largest IT suppliers; makes far more than the search engine it is known for

name: Mozilla
note: A non-profit foundation rather than a company in the usual sense

name: Microsoft
note: Makes an operating system, a browser and a search engine — a good reason not to equate a maker with one kind of thing

name: Apple
note: Makes devices, an operating system and a browser

name: Apache Software Foundation
note: A foundation, not a firm — the same distinction Mozilla already makes in this list, and a reason a maker is not always a company

name: Signal Foundation
note: A non-profit; the thing it makes is often named as if it were the organisation. And it carries no German article for exactly that reason: de.wikipedia redirects „Signal Foundation" to the article about the APP. A redirect is not always a canonical title — sometimes it is a change of category, and following it here would assert that the maker and the thing it makes are one page.

name: Telegram (company)
note: The firm and the app carry the same name, which is exactly the confusion this system is about — and it made the explanation read „Telegram ist ein Messenger von Telegram." The suffix is a DISAMBIGUATION of this inventory, not part of the name: the legal entity is Telegram FZ-LLC / Telegram Messenger Inc., which is not written here because it is not verified. No row of this system may assert something unchecked. For the same reason it carries no Wikipedia article: both wikis have only ONE Telegram page and it is about the software, so pointing the company at it would assert the very confusion the quiz asks about.

name: Wikimedia Foundation
note: A non-profit that runs Wikipedia and does not write it — the sharpest maker/thing case after Telegram, and the reason this one is in the inventory at all

name: Meta
note: Owns the messenger most phones carry — and is named nothing like it, which is the whole point of asking

name: OpenAI
note: Makes ChatGPT. The firm and the thing have different names, unlike Telegram — a useful contrast in one inventory

name: Anthropic
note: Makes Claude. Same shape as OpenAI and ChatGPT: a maker nobody would guess from the product name
